messages:
elena: FYI i just found a partner log dump that includes a base64 KMS-wrapped ciphertext field. looks like the partner forwarded ingestion logs to our archive bucket.
elena: sample (redacted): `CiQAB3X...==` — starts with the usual KMS prefix, so may contain an SA key.
taylor: which partner & which pipeline? need to know blast radius before we call them.
elena: partner: tidebridge-integration. pipeline: partner-ingest-gcs -> log-forwarder. log line has partner_payload.kms_blob
samir: ok, two immediate concerns: 1) the wrapped blob may contain secrets 2) partner might still have plaintext if they forwarded raw payloads. we should assume compromise until proven otherwise.
oncall: creating an incident ticket and paging partner contact. tagging sec-oncall. (reacted with :rotating_light:)
vault-bot: incident INC-2026 created and linked to this thread
samir: proposed triage steps (short):
- ask partner to stop forwarding raw logs and delete the uploaded object
- rotate any SA/credentials that could be in the blob
- rewrap ciphertext with a new ephemeral WRAP key and verify plaintext contents in a locked environment
- tighten Vault/KMS RBAC to remove partner-unwrap capability
- export vault/unseal and kms decrypt audit logs for timeframe
taylor: agree. additions: require partner to provide proof-of-deletion (GCS object audit entry or signed S3 delete) and timestamp. also we should push a short-term permission gate in IAM to block decrypt from the service account used by the log-forwarder.
elena: i already messaged partner legal and their security contact. they said they will rotate keys if we confirm exposure. i asked for the object id and deletion proof.
oncall: i've temporarily revoked the log-forwarder service-account key in GCP for the ingest project — will re-enable only after rotation.
samir: commands we ran / recommend for internal verification (share with ops):
```
# list candidate KMS decrypt attempts
gcloud logging read "resource.type=kms_crypto_key AND protoPayload.methodName:decrypt" --freshness=1d
# list GCS object access to archive-bucket
gcloud logging read "resource.type=gcs_bucket AND protoPayload.resourceName:projects/_/buckets/archive-bucket/objects/partner-dumps*" --limit=50
```
(taylor: copied the snippets into the incident ticket)
elena: on content: if the wrapped blob decodes to a JSON with keys, treat it as high-sev. plan to run decryption in a locked build agent with MFA and audit on. need an approver for plaintext unwrapping: @taylor
taylor: approved, but only in the secure staging environment. samir, can you run the unwrapping and checksum the result and paste a summary (no secret material) back here?
samir: yes. i'll do the unwrap on a short-lived VM with no external egress, capture a SHA256 of the plaintext and then shred the VM. timeframe ~2 hours.
oncall: RBAC follow-up: i'm rolling a policy that removes the role projects/*/locations/*/keyRings/*/cryptoKeys/*/cryptoKeyVersions/*:cloudkms.cryptoKeyVersions.useToDecrypt for the log-forwarder SA. will apply and monitor for regressions.
taylor: also enable Vault audit forwarding to our long-term retention for the last 7 days and run a quick grep for partner SA identity in the audit stream.
elena: timeline summary:
- 00:10 partner asked to delete + provide proof
- 00:20 revoked log-forwarder SA
- 02:00 samir to produce plaintext checksum + classification
- 04:00 rotate internal wrap keys and rewrap any affected objects
- 24:00 postmortem + policy changes
elena: tagging this thread for follow-up: please update INC-2026 with each step. i'll coordinate partner comms. :white_check_mark:
vault-bot: scheduled rewrap job queued (requires manual kick) — see INC-2026
samir: will update here after unwrap and checksum. starting now.
